utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. With your permission, I would like to make a correction to yesterday's transcript, line -- page 4744, line 1 should read Exhibit number 1D110 and on page 4783 line 1 exhibit number should read 1D111. Thank you. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Thank you, Mr. Alarid, because we were just in the process of considering a hearing on Monday afternoon but that would not fit in with your proofing.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In terms of a hearing, are we talking about a housekeeping hearing or a -- JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: No, the witness that you had intended to call.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: No, I would like to get that out of the way. If we could get it out of the way, I would do that. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Because in the process of seeing whether we can do have swap with another court and to have the hearing on the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I would prefer to get the witness done. I think it's important to keep it going as much as we could. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: How much time do you anticipate for that witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I think we could get him done within the court session. It would be the court session. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: The whole afternoon?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just with the issues surrounding him in the past with the Court, I can't anticipate and the Prosecution may have, you know, its opportunity. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Okay, very well but we are in the process of examining that and we will know, I hope, after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Wonderful. Thank you, Your Honour. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Are you ready to bring the next witness now?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe it's the cross-examination of MLD22.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: MLD22, my name is Stevan Cole. I will be asking you some questions today on behalf of the Prosecution. My first question to you today is for you -- in fact, Your Honours, if we could go into private session for this first group of questions, please. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Private, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'm going to now about meeting Milan Lukic and can you tell the Court when you first met Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him when he came back from Switzerland, a neighbour of mine came and he came, and he was in the reserve police force and that's how I saw him. That's how we met.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Is this in the year of 1992 that you first met him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, 1992. I can't specify the date or the month, but it was in 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, you say that he was in the reserve police force. How do you know he was a member of the reserve police force?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I know, I saw him with the Commander Tomic and the other policemen who were living in Visegrad at the time or rather were serving in the Visegrad police.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How do you know that he was a member of the reserve police as opposed to the regular police?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know because of my neighbour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So is it your evidence that your neighbour told you that Milan Lukic was in the reserve police?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: When was the first time you saw Milan Lukic in a police uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, sir. I can't remember more specifically than that. I had a lot of my own work to look after in the medical unit, so I saw people around not just Milan but other police officers who were making sure the town was as safe as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you give us a description of the uniform that you saw Milan Lukic wearing in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the uniform was the same as that one worn by all the others, the police commander and the reservists; it was a blue police uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What else can you tell us about the uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a beret as well with a three-coloured flag and that was about all there was to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did the uniform have the word "police" or a police badge on it somewhere?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it said "milicija".

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Whereabouts did you see that word on the uniform?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was on the shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, you indicated the upper arm, do you mean it was on the upper arm or was it on the shoulder?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Somewhere between the upper arm and the shoulder.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And for the record, I note you were indicating with your left hand the area of your upper arm, that is between the elbow and the shoulder; do you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's something like that, it depended on how a uniform fitted a particular person. Not all people were the certain size, you know, sometimes it could be further up the upper arm as it were and sometimes lower down.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, you spoke of being mobilised and being based at the Bikavac hotel, but you also mentioned certainly in the English transcript, the Bikavac restaurant, so hotel and restaurant. So my question there is: Were you talking about the same place when you were talking about the Bikavac hotel and restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, when we say restaurant, we mean kitchen where I come from, and it's all part of this hotel, sir, if you get my meaning.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Right. So you were based at the Bikavac hotel from the date of your mobilisation in 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, sir, judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please, how far is the Bikavac hotel from the old bridge over the Drina and the town square?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure how to say this. Do you mean taking the road or do you mean as the crow flies?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, if you walk from the Bikavac hotel to the old bridge, how long is it going to take you to get there or to the town square?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Five to ten minutes normal pace.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, yesterday, when we were in the other courtroom when Mr. Ivetic first asked you about the date of your mobilisation, you firstly said that you were mobilised on the 19th of March, 1992. I'm just going to read back the passage from yesterday to remind you, so please listen carefully. It's page 4813, lines 12 to 20: "Q. Sir, turning to the outbreak of hostilities in Visegrad in 1992, were you mobilised at that time? "A. I was mobilised on or about the 19th of March, 1992 and was sent to Bikavac, the restaurant there. The restaurant had sustained a great deal of damage, and I used my technical expertise to get the place up and running again, clear it up to make sure the conditions were again sanitary and safe for everyone. I was responsible for that." Question from Mr. Ivetic: "Could we back up and could you please confirm for us the date when it was that you were mobilised and sent to the Bikavac restaurant?" Now that's -- just a moment, please. Just hold it, and I will ask you something. Now, that's the passage from yesterday. You then corrected yourself as to the date and you said at lines 21 and 22, this is your answer: "The date was 19th of March -- May -- May, I'm sorry, the 19th of May. My apologies, but time seems to have left a mark on my memory." Now, I've just read you the transcript from yesterday. Now, when you corrected yourself from saying the 19th of March to saying the 19th of May, for the date of your mobilisation, I'm going to suggest this was because you heard the accused Milan Lukic say the date from where he was sitting in the courtroom yesterday. That's my suggestion to you. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Judge, it was a knee-jerk reaction, and I got the month wrong. I can document this if I ever get back home alive because I see that planes are falling from the sky all over the place these days. I can send you all the appropriate documents, I have my military notebook. You can see all the dates there, and that will prove my point. I simply got the date wrong, but that wasn't a deliberate error. I can still assert responsibly that it happened on the 19th of May, 1992; reporting at 9.00, I even remember the time of day and I'll never be able to forget that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Just a moment. The point of my question was, MLD22, that you were able to correct yourself yesterday with a little bit of help from the accused who gave you the date. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I took an oath. It was simply something that I got wrong. It was not a deliberate error. Please excuse me for that. I do have the documents to back my claim up. It's about the letter M, all of it, month, March, May, my throat feeling a bit dry with tension, all these problems that I am facing. Please try to understand my situation appearing as a witness here.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. We'll move on now. So do I understand your evidence correctly that you were based at the Bikavac hotel from the 19th of May, 1992, and that at some later date you were sent to the Zupa area near the village of Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At Bikavac, I was in charge of hygiene and accommodation and then this mate of mine who was a male nurse was killed somewhere on the ground in Rujiste village, and then I drove there to replace him. He had just been killed and I continued working --

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If I can just interrupt you, we will be able to shorten things a little bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness be allowed to complete his answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honours I'm going to be asking further about this now. I'm not chopping him off now. It's just that if we're going to get long answers like this, we're going to be here for a longer period of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: The witness was simply responding to the question as best he could.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, MLD22, I'll put the question to you again. I'm interested in the timings here. You were at the Bikavac hotel from the 19th of May, 1992, and some time after that, and I'm going to ask you about it, you were sent to the Zupa area near the village of Rujiste, have we got that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And the reason that you went to the Rujiste area is because a male nurse called Stevo Grujic was killed somewhere in that area, and you replaced him; have we got that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is right, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, the first name Stevo, is that short for Stevan, S-t-e-v-a-n?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: How many days after the death of Stevan Grujic did you arrive -- did you actually arrive in the Rujiste area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember the day with precision, but it was within a few days that I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And can you tell us how far Rujiste is from Visegrad both in time to get there in a car and the distance?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, whether it was 24 or 26 kilometres to the positions, believe me, I never measured, but it is thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: About how long to drive there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It takes an hour or so, an hour and ten minutes, 70 minutes in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And did your unit have a name or number, the part of the unit, the unit that were part of at Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, you'd been mobilised, you were part of a force that was sent to Rujiste. Did this group have an army number or a regimental number, something like that or a name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may have been called the 1st Company or the Zupa Unit or something of that sort.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So how far was your unit or your group from the front line or action with the enemy during the time that you were there near Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That unit just held the position in order to prevent any clashes from occurring. It held the right bank of the Drina from the Brusnicki creek in the direction of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, what I'm asking, how far away was the nearest enemy action to where you were?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation. Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, it may be a speculative answer that's coming but let's wait and hear it from him, Your Honour. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Answer the question, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know, Your Honours. Well, the Drina is the border. The Drina is quite wide there, and the border follows the line towards [indiscernible] and so on and so forth. I don't know. It is quite forbidding terrain. The canyon is there too, and I can only speculate, and you are a Court. I can't do that. I cannot say with precision. I am in charge of hygiene of medical matters, I wasn't interested in these things, believe me. What was my concern was that the troops should be healthy, and that was my duty and those were my problems, my concerns.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, certainly you would be interested where the enemy were, wouldn't you, how close they were?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, relevance.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, Stevan Grujic, before you went to Rujiste in 1992 as you've been telling the Court, had you met this man before or did you know him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Stevan Grujic was a technician in Visegrad, and he worked as a male nurse in this medical unit. I know him personally, and I'm very sorry for the man. He was a decent fellow, a good citizen, a good colleague, a good associate, a friend.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Now, Stevan Grujic, the year that he would have been born, would that be 1940, would that be about right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't say with precision. I can't testify to that because I just don't know. But he was a senior technician.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, if we're talking about 1992 when you knew him, was he about 50 at that stage?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, asked and answered. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Mr. Cole, can you give us a time estimate because the examination-in-chief had 18 minutes, and you have now had something like more than half an hour; and we still have three witnesses or two witnesses this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Actually only one, Your Honour. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Only one, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I hope I can conclude this in 20 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I was asking you about Mr. Grujic and would he have been about the age -- you said you knew him personally, would he have been about 50 when you knew him in 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you say so, let it be so. I cannot guess. I don't know. I really don't know. Whether he looks young, that's something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you confirm for us, then, that the area that he was killed was in the vicinity of Klasnik a little bit south of Rujiste. I'll spell that, K-l-a-s- with a mark over it -n-i-k.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, my learned friend, Mr. Alarid, is making some, what I would describe as, objections that don't have any basis. It's a -- and it's happening time and time again. It's a matter that may well be within the province of this witness, and we won't know until he's allowed to give an answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Then he can ask him if he knows, but the fact of the matter is, is he wasn't there so he's asking him to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're allowed to ask the witness and effectively what it is, is the basis of the testimony that he gave yesterday that he replaced this man because he was killed. Now it may be that he has a lot of further information that about this that we don't know about, and, with respect, I'm entitled to ask him further questions in this area. It may be that he can assist the Court here. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: I will allow the questions, Mr. Cole. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: MLD22, can you confirm that it was in the general area of Klasnik south of Rujiste that you understand Mr. Grujic was killed?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was killed on the road, that is what I learned, but, sir, I wasn't there. I cannot know with precision. I only know that people have placed flowers on the spot to mark the spot where he was killed. This is our custom. So that is there.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, sir. The flowers are placed in the Klasnik area, that's what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the road there, and I would not say anything further about it in order not to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on and see if we can finish these questions promptly. So is it your evidence that you saw the parents of Milan Lukic on a regular basis during the time that you were posted at Rujiste, in that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I had to see them when I was touring the unit, the men were in dug-outs, in tents and I had to see them because they would come sometimes to get some food, they would come carrying some utensils and such.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Could I just ask you if you could, try and limit your answers to short answers, if you could, please. How long were you posted to this Rujiste area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know exactly. I cannot remember. It was for quite a while.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Can you give us some assistance, was it one month, three, six months, a year? How long?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was over a year.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And is it your evidence that on some occasions you saw Milan Lukic visiting his parents during that period of a year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, normally, sir, everyone wants to see one's parents, one's mother and one's father, and to see what kind of health condition they are in and generally how they are. And after all, it was the front line, there were no sources of food. The spot was inaccessible. One had to get the food and other necessities there.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could I just ask, please, that you try and keep your answers short if you can, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that the witness be shown a set of documents on the list that I have submitted. It's the Milan Lukic 65 ter number 5. And I'm going to ask that two pages be displayed at the same time, one in B/C/S and one in English. 65 ter number 5, the document number 1D21-0479 and the B/C/S is ERN 0213-2847. The English version 1D21-0483, the English ERN 0213-2851.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, in a moment, MLD22, you're going to see a list of names come up on the screen in front of you, and I want you to have a look, please, at item number 59 on the list.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute. Let me get my glasses. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: We are told that the documents were not released, and that it may take some time for them to be uploaded.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Very well. I'll move on with questions, Your Honour, and perhaps an indication when it's available and I can go back to that. Our case manager has indicated the document number that will assist is 0213-2844, that must be the main number. All right. I'll move on with the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, that may need to be redacted, and we should be in private session. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Do you want to go in private session, is that what you ask?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, in fact, it -- if that could be redacted, that question and answer and then we can remain in open session, thank you. Your Honour, perhaps we can now deal with the documents that are on the screen and if I can ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you see a document on the screen in front of you, MLD22, it's number 59 and can you see that on the screen?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And that, correct me if I am wrong, indicates that Stevan Grujic, born 1940 from Koritnik was killed at Klasnik on the 28th of August, 1992; is that what it says?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says, Mr. Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you can see the small photo there of number 59, does that seem to be the Stevan Grujic that you knew?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photograph is quite fuzzy, it's slightly damaged, but it is Stevan Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And the details that you can see alongside that little photograph there, can you confirm that that information accords with your recollection that Stevan Grujic would have been killed on about the 28th of August, 1992, at Klasnik?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. I believe that misstates the evidence already presented. I believe the witness already testified as to his recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: This is -- JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Can you tell us how it misstates the evidence, Mr. Alarid? I don't see your point.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, in looking at the question itself, it specifically says: Can you confirm that this information accords with your recollection that Stevan Grujic would have been killed on or about the 28th of August, 1992, at Klasnik. He never gave a date or a time. He specifically stated he could not do that. Or the date is not his recollection. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Can you clarify that, Mr. Cole?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, when he was asked about this before, he didn't have this information. He now has this information and it's, with respect, permissible to put this to him and see if that accords with his recollection, and that's what I'm doing. I should be allowed to ask that question. Thank you, Your Honour. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: You can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: MLD22, you can see the details about the death of Stevan Grujic. Let's go through it point by point. Do you have any reason to believe that the date of the 28th of August, 1992, is not correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Judge, you can write whatever you like, but I simply cannot recollect the exact date. I'm saying the truth and only the truth. It is very difficult for me to recall that time given all the traumas and the difficulties that I have gone through, I cannot remember the dates with precision. It is stated here the way you put it, but I cannot recall it myself. Many things have happened since.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What I'm asking you, MLD22, is there any reason that you would dispute that date, any reason it can't be that date?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, asked and answered. I believe the last answer suffices. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: I would disagree with that, Mr. Alarid. Please proceed, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Witness, you have the dates in front of you, the date of death, the 28th of August, 1992. Is there any reason that you know of that that date must be or is incorrect, 28 August 1992?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you claim, Mr. Judge, that that is correct, then let it be so, but as far as I'm concerned, I cannot say. Perhaps other people have conveyed other information to you. I cannot say with precision and please do not torment me in this regard.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Then let's use the date, the 28th of August, 1992. If you arrived in the Rujiste area a couple of days or so after the death of Mr. Grujic, that -- it follows, doesn't it, that you were in that area from, let's say, September -- early September 1992 to about September 1993; would that be right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it was longer or shorter than that because as I said before, after all these traumas and ordeals, I didn't actually record those dates I cannot confirm with precision any of them. I was there for over a year or so, and that is what I have said to you, and please take that as the information that I'm able to give you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, could I ask that this document be admitted into evidence and given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, lack of foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document is part of the Defence 65 ter exhibit list, it's number 5. The witness has indicated that the photo appears to be of a man who he has named in his evidence in chief. He's confirmed the place of death, and he hasn't contradicted the date of death. There's more than enough with -- in my submission, for this document now to go into evidence. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: What is the source, what is the origin of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: As I have indicated, it is on the Defence 65 ter exhibit list, and I believe that we, that is the Office of the Prosecutor, did disclose this as part of the materials that were disclosed. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Who is the source of the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: The source of the document is through VG-59 as I understand it, who was one of the original Prosecution witnesses. He hasn't been called, but he produced this document to an investigator, I think, about 2001, came into our possession then. So that's the track record of the document as I know it, and certainly the Defence intends or have indicated they intended to rely on it in some way. So it's a matter of weight, I suppose, in due course, once it's to be considered in due course by the Court. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Yes, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, the 65 ter list is often expansive because we have notification requirements, but we couldn't lay a foundation for this nor authenticate the documents, so that becomes a problem. Not being able to do such, we probably will never introduce this and unless the witness can lay a foundation as to authenticate the document, the Prosecutor cannot be a witness and testify to that history even if it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: We will mark it for identification at this stage, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P246 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, MLD22, do you know Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. Beyond the scope of direct examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. DIECKMANN
utterances.text: Just for the record, we join this objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, this was I think -- this was -- this objection was raised yesterday and dealt with as well. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Yes, we have already ruled on that so please proceed, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: The question is: Do you know Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And who is he?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic was a member of the police of the city of Visegrad. Actually, he worked in the police station of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: When did you last see Sredoje Lukic before today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, was it in the 1990s or since the year 2000?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge ... JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not quite clear on what your question was. Actually, it didn't get through the headphones.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you just give us some idea when it was you last saw Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him on Visegrad television as a prisoner, tortured person, sorely tortured person.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And that's the last time you saw him; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I cannot tell you with precision. I do not remember. It was in 1993 or 1994, I believe. I'm not sure. I cannot give you a precise answer because I was on the front line, the police were doing their work, I was doing my work. I can only guess, if that is to be done. If not, then I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. And Milan Lukic, when was the last time you saw him in person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Difficult to say. I saw him when he came to visit his parents, when he brought them food and coffee and drinks, that sort of thing, medicine.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So what are you saying, that it was around 1993 that you last saw Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Just one last area that I want to ask you some questions about. Who was the first person to contact you on behalf of the Milan Lukic defence in relation to testifying in this trial?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember, a man who struck me as an athlete arrived from America some place, a basketball player, you say, perhaps a lawyer of sorts, something. I don't know what he was called.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So are you saying the first contact you had was from someone in person as opposed to a phone call, this person arrived to speak with you in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He came there, and he spoke to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I just want to be clear. Was this the first contact you had from somebody about testifying in this trial when this person arrived to speak with you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first contact, Mr. Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And was this person a man -- a very tall man called Vladimir Rasic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tall, yes, an athlete. Was it him? Was it not him? It probably was, if you say so; but it's difficult for me to commit. He was into basketball, one of those judges there or some sort or other. But was he or was he not, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: The person that we're talking about, is he the person that went with you to the MUP building to sign a written statement and get it certified? Are we talking about the same person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't go to the MUP building. I went to the municipality building, to one of the offices there. I made a statement there. We both signed it, had it stamped, and we parted ways. I headed back to my work and this other man had other business to conduct elsewhere, so there you have it. I never wanted to have too much to do with those judges there, so they worked me over a little -- well, you know how that goes but I had no choice, really, did I?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I just want to clear this with you. Was it on this first occasion that this tall man came to see you? Was it on that same occasion that you went to the municipality building to get your statement, written statement certified on that very first occasion?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you signed a typed statement, and the official put an official stamp on the statement; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And that was the first time you heard from anyone from the Milan Lukic Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So when this gentleman spoke to you on that first occasion, did he have a typed-up statement ready for you to sign?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He asked me questions and wrote it down, all of it. I told him what I knew, and I stand by that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did he type up the statement in your presence?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gentlemen, he was writing something. Was it in English? Was it in Serbian? I really don't know. But he took this statement and probably had it typed up later, perhaps something or other, he wasn't there with me in the office any longer. Whatever it was that he did, he then brought it back. We both signed it. That was that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So you're saying that after speaking to you, he went away and typed the statement up; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what do you expect me to say? There is -- there are certain kinds of technology that are used for typing up letters, aren't there? You can make a statement through these faxes, monitors, all these gadgets. What do I know? I don't really know much about that. I gave the statement. The man wrote it down. I signed it, that sort of thing. He gave me a sheet of paper to write the statement down to confirm was that it, no, yes, yes, okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Are you saying that you wrote a longhand statement also in addition to this typed statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Judge, of course he asked me, Do you know Milan Lukic? Yes, sir. Do you know Milan Lukic? He wrote it. I didn't write it. I just confirmed what he wrote. I think that's the best way of putting it, just for you to be perfectly clear, you and everyone else around this courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well it's not quite clear. I wonder if you could just explain to us what you actually wrote down.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection. Asked and answered. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Don't interfere, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I apologise, excuse me. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Please don't interfere with the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, page 25, line 2 to line 8 appears to be an answer and then also line 11 to line 14 continues the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Witness, page 25, line 5, line 6 -- that sort of thing, he gave me a sheet of paper to write this statement down, to confirm that -- you indicated in your evidence earlier that you wrote something down in response to this man, and I'd like you to tell us what it was that you wrote down.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I wrote down to have it for myself what I gave him, Mr. Judge, because how will I now write -- you can write something to the effect of Zoran killed someone, but then Zoran didn't, and then the clerk certifies this, puts a stamp on it. I write down for my own benefit what I gave to him, and he takes away what I stated for him. Are you now clear about what I did? I'm sorry that I don't have the note that I made for my benefit with me now. What I knew, what I stated as to what I knew about Milan Lukic, the statement that I wrote, well, if you are clear now, I think it should be sufficiently clear to everyone now. I don't think this would warrant much further comment from anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, I'm almost finished with my questions for you, but I'm afraid I'm not clear, so if we could just clear it up before I finish. Number one, you signed a typewritten statement, which was stamped at the municipal office. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yeah, you can keep that in that case, Mr. Judge, let's put it that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I just want to do this in steps, and the first thing is, I want you to confirm that you signed a typed-up written statement which was certified at the public office; have we got that right?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what other documents did you write? What other document did you write on that same occasion that you either kept or which this man from the Milan Lukic team took away with him?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The same statement that I signed, the same that the lawyer took away. I had that same statement on me, Mr. Judge. If only I had a copy of that statement to keep it from being misused by this Tribunal. And I think now you should be perfect clear about this, you including all those present in this courtroom, sir. Why should I go on talking about that? I've crossed all this way to be here and now, now, we are having an exchange of opinions as to whether this was the case or not. Sure thing. A man must keep a copy of a statement that had a man has made, so, of course, I've got one too.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So what you're saying now is the only thing you wrote down was your signature on a typed statement; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, misstates the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: That's an easy question, isn't it? Is the only thing you wrote your signature on that typed statement?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've almost finished here.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What other members of the Milan Lukic Defence team have you met in person?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What do you mean? Here, or generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Before you arrived here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I saw that first lawyer who came, and then another lawyer came, an American or something. I don't really know. Believe me, I don't have a very good head for names.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Was that other person Mr. Ivetic that came to see you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: When did he come to see you?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Just before my departure to have my statement confirmed to make sure that I stood by my previous statement, and I said, Yes, sir. I had to leave work when he came to speak to me. And then I went back to work because our pay is based on performance.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What month was it that you saw Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was it January or thereabouts?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: That's January this year?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And finally, have you met Jelena Rasic from the Milan Lukic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Your Honours, I have no further questions. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Thank you, Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I release the witness, Your Honour, no further questions. MLD22, we thank you for attending to testify here, and the Milan Lukic team appreciates your presence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, too. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Judge David observes that on line 28, 18 the answer of the witness has not been recorded. Have you met Jelena Rasic from the Lukic team? What was the answer it's not recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, I understood the answer from the witness to be no, a negative. Perhaps we could just clarify that. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I'll ask him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: MLD22, it appears the answer to the last question was not recorded so I'll ask you again. Have you met Jelena Rasic, a member of the Milan Lukic Defence team?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS MLD22 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Thank you very much. Witness, that brings your evidence to an end. We thank you for coming to The Hague and if you wait just a few minutes, this Chamber will rise and then you will be allowed to go. We are going to have the break now. We will have a break of half an hour, so we will resume just after 4.00.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: With apologies, Your Honour, apologies. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: It should be redacted. So Mr. Alarid, what is your answer to this?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I would say that that submission by the Defence supports our arguments. The first question is why is it relevant to this case? And the second submission is are they calling one Defence witness to challenge the evidence of another Defence witness? JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, the Defence of Milan Lukic calls Mr. Miodrag Mitrasinovic. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: While we are waiting for the witness to arrive, a housekeeping matter. We have tried to accommodate you, Mr. Alarid, but we've not been able to move the case to the afternoon, so we won't be able to hear your witness on Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, well then I would apologise and just simply say we're simply going to have to deal with our next witness and I'll try and squeeze that witness in as best I can in the next couple weeks, I'd say. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Good afternoon, Witness. Will you please read the affirmation on the paper that is held before you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly swear that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Thank you very much. You may sit down. You may sit down. Now Mr. Alarid is going to ask you a few questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Mitrasinovic.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: As you may recall, my name is Jason Alarid, I met with you earlier this morning for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you are being recorded, and I know the translators are going to have to hear you, and I can hear that you speak very softly. You will have to speak up for your testimony; okay?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: How are you feeling today?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Have you ever testified in court before?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you're testifying today in open session without protective measures. Now, because of the fact that we are proceeding with an interpreter, it is very important that if you do not understand a particular question of mine or the Prosecutor's or the Court's that you let us know and we can repeat our question; is that acceptable to you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, to begin with, please state your full name for the Court, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Miodrag Mitrasinovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when and where were you born?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: The 18th of November, 1960 in Prelovska Rijeka near Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how old does that make you today?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And can you tell us where your educational background, where you started school, where you went to school.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I went to secondary school, lock smith. I went to elementary school in Prelovo, and then to Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And please again, what village are you from near Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Prelovska Rijeka.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how far away is that from Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: 14 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And, of course, the -- this case here surrounds the war in 1992, but tell us about when you left secondary school and what you did after that.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I finished when I was 18 and then I was off to the army, and after the army I got a job in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And so when you left secondary school, you were about 18 years old, that's correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, thereabouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Okay. And tell us about your compulsory military service; where did you serve?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I served in Croatia on the island of Vis and then in Split.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And how long was your -- and when was your compulsory military service?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And after 1980, what did you do with yourself?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I worked in a tractor factory in New Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What was the name of that factory, if you can recall?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: IMT, the tractor motor industry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And are you married?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I used to be, but I am now divorced.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Do you have any children?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, a son.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And were you married in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Divorced.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, just before the war, were you living in Visegrad or were you living in New Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Surcin, more specifically.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And in 1992, what brought you back to Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, when the clashes broke out, my grandfather was killed in 1941 by the Muslims, so that normally just like any person hailing from those parts in order to prevent history from repeating itself, I went there to defend my homestead.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, where are you living presently today?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Presently, I'm living in Podgorica.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what is your current occupation?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I work in a construction company, the road and bridges building part of the company.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when the war broke out in Bosnia, were you mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Initially we were just village guards, and then later, I joined the Army of Republika Srpska when we were mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can you recall when you were mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Sometime around the 15th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And why do you recall that specifically?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I recall the beginning very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Tell us about the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I can do that. We were assigned to different elevation points. I was at Putina Stijene [phoen] for a while, then they shifted me to Gornja Lijeska to Han Brdo, Sjemensko Polje [phoen], and these places.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: What structure mobilised you, what part of the military structure were you part of?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Infantry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you recall who your commander was?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Pero Kovacevic was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And what kind of uniforms did you wear during your military service?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, everyone wore what they had. We had olive-drab uniforms, we had camouflage uniforms. It was the beginning of the war so not all the uniforms were uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And do you remember what unit you were part of specifically?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I was in the Intervention Platoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And prior to the war, did you know Milan Lukic at all?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: When was the first time you came to know of Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I met Milan towards the end of the war when he opened his cafe, his bar.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And understanding that that's when you knew Milan personally, tell me when the first time you knew of him.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, believe me, that was the time I heard of him. We had never -- or had seldom met before that. We didn't know each other. I was in one platoon, he was in another one and we were at different elevation points.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the platoon you were in, what company were you -- the Intervention Brigade, how many men are in the Intervention Brigade?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the Intervention Brigade comprised four Intervention Platoons, there were over 100 men there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so approximately how many men were assigned to each platoon?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it depended, 30 or more than that or less than that. It depended on the specific case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, at what point in time was it your understanding that Milan Lukic became part of the larger Intervention Brigade or company?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know. I do not remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, specifically, you'd like to ask you -- you say you were mobilised about the 15th of May; is that correct? And that's 1992.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And tell us how you were mobilised, what did the system do to you so that you became mobilised?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I reported up there at the command, and then they assigned me to my position.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Can we go into private session, Your Honour. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, specifically understanding that you, ultimately, were in the same company in the Intervention Brigade with Milan Lukic, did you ever have any time to actually fight with him or were you apart?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No, we never were together, we were perhaps quite near one another, trick point, another trick point; but we never acted together.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Did you know of a scout unit with Sladjan Simic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I had heard of that unit, but we had no occasion to participate in any actions together.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, when were you first approached to be a witness by -- related to the Milan Lukic case?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Some time this autumn.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And who came to meet you?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Jelena Rasic did.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And tell us about what you did during that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I was down there in Podgorica at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And were you made aware about the accusations against you related to the Sase junction and the Drina River?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I was -- rather I had heard about it, and that is why I came here in order to clear my name.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Is that why you're speaking here without protective measures?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And since that meeting, had you ever been able to meet with a lawyer from the Defence team such as myself or Mr. Ivetic, who you met with this morning?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I had a meeting for the first time this morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And so it's fair to say that you had not met an attorney for the team until today?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No, I had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, as part of our proofing session, I showed you a statement that you gave to Bosnian authorities, correct, in 2002?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I don't know if we need to bring it up, Your Honour, but maybe just to have it available, ERN 0646-6387, a two-page document ending at 0646-6388. Could we go to the second page, please, and the signature for the witness. Is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now, tell us about the circumstances of your being called in for a statement in 2002.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they called me --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter is not quite sure she heard the witness properly. Could the answer please be repeated.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Sir, could you please repeat yourself. The interpreter could not hear you.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: They called me in connection with a hijacking of the train and in that connection, I gave the statement. That is why I was contacted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And you had a chance to read your statement this morning, do you need any more time to read it today or are you comfortable talking about it?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No problem. That's okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Tell the Court in summary what you had to say about that train incident?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know anything about it, and that is actually what I stated in this written statement of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Have you ever been charged with a crime in relation to that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Have you ever been charged with a crime?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I showed you some photographs this morning to see if you could remember them. Do you remember those photographs?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I can't say, it was the very beginning. I'm not quite sure. Well, we had some photographs taken, I don't see how bad that can be.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Just in reviewing those photographs, do you remember when or where they were taken?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, can we know which photographs are being referred to?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: They are part of the Srevren [phoen] photographs. And since I can't recognise them as a young man, I forget which ones I showed him; I showed him the entire set, so that becomes an issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: In those photographs, you saw yourself, did you not, on a couple of those?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, two or three of them. I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Now in those photographs, at least, there is some inference that Milan Lukic was in the general area or part of the photographs; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And I'm sure the Prosecution is going to ask you in a little while as to how you didn't know Mr. Milan Lukic better at that time if you are in photographs in proximity to him. What do you have to say about that?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I do have lots of photographs with lots of soldiers whom I don't know, but they are with me in photographs. And they have my photographs without necessarily knowing me.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: You'll ask you one last time before I release you as a witness: Did you participate in the killing at the Drina River on 7 June 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I have no further questions of this witness at this time, Your Honour. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Thank you, Mr. Alarid. Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrasinovic, good afternoon. My name is Maxine Marcus, and I will be asking you some questions on behalf of the Prosecution today. In 1992, you were approximately 32 years old. Would you say that's correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And you were, as you have testified today, a member of the Republika Srpska army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, the dates of your military service were from, as you've said, approximately the 15th of May, 1992, through until 1995; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Would you agree that during the months of April, May and June of 1992, there was active armed combat in the area in Visegrad and the surrounding municipalities?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: There were provocations on their part. There were attacks on Serbian villages and such.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, to your knowledge, would it have been possible for someone to be fighting under the VRS command while simultaneously serving as, let's say, a mobilised police officer?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection calls for speculation, lack of foundation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Well, I asked him to his knowledge, he can say he doesn't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: My question was: According to your knowledge, would it have been possible for someone to have been fighting under the VRS command while simultaneously serving as a mobilised police officer?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, the police, too, was part of the Army of Republika Srpska. It participated like the other troops.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you returned to Visegrad in the first half of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And you voluntarily joined the VRS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: You testified that you were in the Intervention Company or the Intervention Unit of the Visegrad Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And in that capacity, you carried an automatic weapon with you, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And you wore a camouflage uniform, did you not?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: At any time, did you wear any uniform or bear any insignia which would have been worn by the police?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I did not understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: My question to you was: At any time, did you wear any uniform or bear any insignia which would have been worn by the police?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: We wore our emblems of the Serbian Army, that is the police had their insignia.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Within the Intervention Company, you were the commander of the 3rd Platoon; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Mitrasinovic, your evidence today was that you did not know Milan Lukic in 1992; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, you testified that you didn't know him personally but did you see him around in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: We may have seen each other, but I didn't know who he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So do you confirm that you saw him around Visegrad in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not sure that I saw him at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Well, when you did see him, can you describe the kind of uniform you saw him wearing?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: When I saw him, when I know for a fact that I did see him was the end of the war. At that time, he was in civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Are you aware of the existence of an armed unit which was led by Milan Lukic in Visegrad in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I'm not aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So your evidence here today is that you are unaware of whether Milan Lukic had his own armed group in Visegrad in 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I am unaware of that fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, as predicted by the Defence, I'm going to show you a few photographs. Could I ask the court officer, please, to call up, please, 1D98. Could I request, please, that we focus on the top photograph first. Mr. Mitrasinovic, do you recognise any of the people in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Could we go to the bottom photograph, please. Now, I'd like to ask you the same question about this photograph. Do you recognise any of the individuals in this photograph?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I only know Mitar Knezevic. I only recognise Mitar Knezevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you tell us which one is Mitar Knezevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: This one here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is it possible to have the witness mark, assisted with marking the photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now can you confirm that the person you've just circled is the person that you've just named as Mitar Knezevic?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: And what, to your knowledge, was his role during the war?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm not quite sure. He was usually among the village guards. I know that his brother's house had been burnt down.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, what unit did he fight in, if you know?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: He wasn't a military conscript. He had lost the sight of one eye, so he was never mobilised.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, the uniform that you see him wearing, was this a kind of a uniform that was standardly worn by the VRS, members of the VRS?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, it's difficult to see. Everybody wore what they could. I don't know where he got this uniform from.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, particularly focussing on his hat, could you confirm that that hat was frequently worn by members of a unit that may have been referred to as the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, lack of foundation.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'm asking him if he can confirm it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: To your knowledge, can you confirm that that hat was frequently worn by members of a unit who may have been referred to as the White Eagles?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that unit, and I didn't see them wear these caps.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, can you identify the person who appears in the back row, second from the left? I'd like you to focus in on that person and see whether you recognise that individual.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I don't know who you mean.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: The back row, the ones who are standing, the second from the left.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: This one over here, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what were the circumstances --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just to let the record reflect, the witness circled the face per the instructions or at least the reference by the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: What were the circumstances in which this photograph was taken?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, this came about with no planning at all involved, to be truthful. There were many soldiers milling about, people were taking photographs. I don't think that's a bad thing in itself for us to be talking photographs of ourselves, is it.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So your evidence is that the persons in this photograph are soldiers; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, misstates the evidence. He specifically testified that the Mitar in the photo was not conscripted due to his eye.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes. In the previous answer he just said, There were many soldiers milling about. People were taking photographs. I don't think it's a bad thing for -- to be taking photographs of ourselves, is it? So I think it leads very clearly from that answer of the witness that he is saying that he and the others were soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, I'd like to return, please, for one more moment to the top photograph. -- is it true that it can't be moved before saved -- sorry, could I please have this entered into evidence. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P247, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now could we call up, I guess, another version of the original document and return to the top photograph, please. Is it possible, please, to zoom in on the person on the right, seated on the right as we look at it, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrasinovic, do you recognise the person sitting there that we're zoomed in on?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you to circle, again, on that photograph, please.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, with -- thank you, with the record reflecting that the witness has circled the person on the right as himself, could I request that this be submitted into evidence as well.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P248, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrasinovic, you did not testify in the case against Mitar Vasiljevic; is that true?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you aware, no doubt -- you were aware no doubt that there was a case against him?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Were you contacted by either the Prosecution or the Defence during that case?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Objection, relevance.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, the witness has brought in evidence which relates directly to evidence relating to the Drina River. Without going farther, in light of circumstances which I think we're aware of, I think it's perfectly proper to ask him about why he hasn't come forward sooner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Then I would object as to lack of foundation as the Prosecution has not established this witness's knowledge or ability to even make that, nor is it the Prosecution established a duty to do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: I have simply asked him whether he was contacted by the Prosecution or the Defence. If his answer is no, I can move forward from there. JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: The witness has said that he knows Mr. Vasiljevic, and I don't see a problem with this question so please proceed, Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrasinovic, were you contacted by either the Prosecution or by the Defence during the Vasiljevic case?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No one contacted me.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Did you follow the evidence in that case?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Can you name this person? If you prefer to do it in private session, we can go into private session for you to name the person.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: I'd prefer not to mention his name.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I request private session? JUDGE VAN DEN WYNGAERT: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Mr. Mitrasinovic, we're in private session now.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, they said that I had been involved in this killing down near the Drina, as you refer to it here.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you just said "they said that I had been involved in this killing down near the Drina." When you say "they," you're referring to the person that you named in private session; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, just earlier when I asked you who told you this, you said it was a man, and in private session, the person whose name you revealed is a woman. Can you clarify that discrepancy?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, a friend could be male or female.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So you're saying that this is a translation problem?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Now, could you elaborate a little bit on what specifically you were told? So you said that she had said you were involved in this killing down by the Drina. What specifically did she say?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
utterances.text: No, she didn't say that. She just said that I had been named.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: So Mr. Mitrasinovic, is it your evidence that you were not involved at all in the Drina River killings on the 7th of June along with Mitar Vasiljevic and Milan Lukic? Is that, in fact, your evidence?

utterances.speaker: MIODRAG MITRASINOVIC
